unit.why: A homiletic discussion about scorn of the righteous and faith in divine providence frames an embedded narrative: the Besht's failed journey toward the Land of Israel to meet the Or ha-Hayyim.
unit.boundary_note: division opens with 'ב)' under the heading 'מענין הגאולה' at the end of the previous division; the narrative is wrapped in a teaching frame

stories.start_quote: כמו שעשו להה״ק ר׳ חיים בן עטר
stories.end_quote: ואתי עמי היה באלה ואלה רבות מיום הולדי
stories.summary_en: The Besht hopes to bring the redemption by meeting R. Hayyim ben Attar (Or ha-Hayyim). He travels toward the Land of Israel against Heaven's warning and is stripped of his spiritual levels in Istanbul. After a shipwreck in which his daughter Adel is endangered and an encounter with Samael, he vows to return, and Ahijah the Shilonite brings him back. The tale is framed by a teaching on accepting suffering with faith.
